items.statement: Production under loan licence or contract, contract analysis and any other GMP activity is correctly defined, agreed and controlled to avoid misunderstandings leading to unsatisfactory quality.
items.quote: Production under loan licence or contract and contract analysis and any other activity covered by good manufacturing practices must be correctly defined, agreed and controlled in order to avoid misunderstandings that could result in a product, or work or analysis, of unsatisfactory quality.

items.statement: All loan licence or contract production and analysis arrangements, including technology transfer and any proposed technical or other changes, conform to the licence for the product concerned.
items.quote: All arrangements for production under loan licence or contract and analysis, including technology transfer and any proposed changes in technical or other arrangements, shall be in accordance with the licence for the product concerned.

items.statement: The contract allows the loan licensee or contract giver to audit the facilities and activities of the facility provider or contract acceptor and of mutually agreed sub-contractors.
items.quote: The contract shall permit the loan licensee or contract giver to audit the facilities and activities of the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor or mutually agreed sub-contractors.

items.statement: For contract analysis, final release approval is given by the authorised person in line with GMP and the licence, as specified in the contract.
items.quote: In the case of contract analysis, the final approval for release must be given by the authorised person in accordance with good manufacturing practices and the licence as specified in the contract.

items.statement: The loan licensee's or contract giver's quality system covers control and review of all outsourced activities.
items.quote: The product quality system of the loan licensee or contract giver shall include the control and review of any outsourced activities.

items.statement: The contract giver assesses the legality, suitability and competence of the facility provider or contract acceptor, approves contract activities, and ensures through the contract that GMP including quality risk management principles are followed.
items.quote: The contract giver is responsible for assessing the legality, suitability and competence of the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor to successfully carry out the work or tests required, for approval for contract activities, and for ensuring by means of the contract that the principles of good manufacturing practices incorporating quality risk management principles are followed.

items.statement: The loan licensee or contract giver gives the facility provider or contract acceptor all information needed to perform the contracted operations correctly per the licence and other legal requirements.
items.quote: The loan licensee or contract giver shall provide the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor with all the information necessary to carry out the contracted operations correctly in accordance with the licence and any other legal requirements.

items.statement: The loan licensee or contract giver makes sure the facility provider or contract acceptor knows of any hazards of the product, work or tests that could put premises, equipment, personnel, other materials or products at risk.
items.quote: The loan licensee or contract giver shall ensure that the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor is fully aware of any hazards associated with the product, work or tests that might pose a risk to premises, equipment, personnel, other materials or other products.

items.statement: The loan licensee or contract giver reviews and assesses the records and results of outsourced activities.
items.quote: The loan licensee or contract giver shall review and assess the records and results related to the outsourced activities.

items.statement: The contract giver ensures all products and materials delivered by the facility provider or contract acceptor were processed per GMP and the licence, meet their specifications, and were released by the authorised person per GMP and the licence.
items.quote: The contract giver shall ensure that all the products and materials delivered by the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor have been processed in accordance with good manufacturing practices and the licence; comply with their specifications and that the product has been released by the authorised person in accordance with good manufacturing practices and the licence.

items.statement: The loan licensee or contract giver monitors and reviews the facility provider's or contract acceptor's performance, including implementation and effectiveness of any needed improvements.
items.quote: The loan licensee or contract giver shall monitor and review the performance of the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor including the implementation of any needed improvements and their effectiveness.

items.statement: The loan licensee or contract giver ensures the facility provider or contract acceptor understands its activities may be inspected by the competent authorities.
items.quote: The loan licensee or contract giver is responsible for ensuring that the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor understands that his or her activities may be subject to inspection by the competent authorities.

items.statement: The facility provider or contract acceptor has adequate premises, equipment, knowledge, experience and competent personnel to carry out the work ordered satisfactorily.
items.quote: The manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor must have adequate premises, equipment, knowledge, experience and competent personnel to satisfactorily carry out the work ordered by the loan licensee or contract giver.

items.statement: Contract manufacture is carried out only by a manufacturer holding a valid manufacturing licence.
items.quote: Contract manufacture shall be undertaken only by a manufacturer who holds a valid manufacturing licence.

items.statement: The facility provider or contract acceptor does not subcontract any entrusted work to a third party unless the loan licensee or contract giver has first evaluated and approved the arrangements.
items.quote: The manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor shall not pass to a third party any of the work entrusted to him or her under the contract without the loan licensee or contract giver’s prior evaluation and approval of the arrangements.
items.condition: before subcontracting to a third party

items.statement: Arrangements between the facility provider or contract acceptor and a third party make information and knowledge, including third-party suitability assessments, available as between the original contract parties.
items.quote: Arrangements made between the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor and any third party shall ensure that information and knowledge, including that from assessments of the suitability of the third party, are made available in the same way as between the original loan licensee or contract giver and contract acceptor.

items.statement: The facility provider or contract acceptor avoids any activity, including unauthorised changes outside the contract terms, that could harm the quality of product made or analysed for the contract giver.
items.quote: The manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor shall refrain from any activity (including unauthorised changes outside the terms of the contract) that may adversely affect the quality of the product manufactured oranalysed or both for the loan licensee or contract giver.

not_applicable.text: samples of the intermediate or API or finished product produced by the modiﬁed process can be placed

items.statement: A written contract between the loan licensee or contract giver and the facility provider or contract acceptor clearly sets each party's responsibilities, covering outsourced activities, related products or operations, communication processes and technical arrangements.
items.quote: There must be a written contract between the loan licensee or contract giver and the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor which clearly establishes the responsibilities of each party, covering the outsourced activities, the products or operations to which they are related, communication processes relating to the outsourced activities and any technical arrangements made in connection with it.

items.statement: The contract clearly states how the authorised person, when releasing each batch or issuing the certificate of analysis, exercises full responsibility and ensures each batch was made and checked in compliance with the licence.
items.quote: The contract must clearly state the way in which the authorised person, in releasing each batch of product for sale or issuing the certificate of analysis, exercises his or her full responsibility and ensures that each batch has been manufactured in, and checked for, compliance with the requirements of the licence.

items.statement: Technical aspects of the contract are drafted by competent persons knowledgeable in pharmaceutical technology, analysis and GMP.
items.quote: Technical aspects of the contract shall be drawn up by competent persons with suitable knowledge of pharmaceutical technology, analysis and good manufacturing practices.

items.statement: All production and analysis arrangements conform to the licence and are agreed by both parties.
items.quote: All arrangements for production and analysis must be in accordance with the licence and agreed by both parties.

items.statement: The contract clearly assigns responsibility for contracted activities (for example knowledge management, technology transfer, supply chain, sub-contracting, testing and release of materials, production and quality control including in-process controls) and for sampling and analysis.
items.quote: The contract shall clearly describe who is responsible for contracted activities e.g., knowledge management, technology transfer, supply chain, sub-contracting, testing and releasing materials and undertaking production and quality control, including in-process controls, and who has responsibility for sampling and analysis.

items.statement: For contract analysis, the contract states whether the facility provider or contract acceptor takes samples at the manufacturer's premises.
items.quote: In the case of contract analysis, the contract shall state whether or not the manufacturing facility provider or contract acceptor shall take samples at the premises of the manufacturer.

items.statement: Manufacturing, analytical and distribution records and reference samples are kept by, or available to, the loan licensee or contract giver.
items.quote: Manufacturing, analytical and distribution records, and reference samples, shall be kept by, or be available to, the loan licensee or contract giver.

items.statement: Records relevant to assessing product quality after complaints or a suspected defect, or to investigating suspected product or laboratory fraud, are accessible and specified in the contract giver's procedures.
items.quote: Any records relevant to assessing the quality of a product in the event of complaints or a suspected defect, or to investigating a suspected product or laboratory fraud, must be accessible and specified in the procedures of the loan licensee or contract giver.
items.condition: complaints, suspected defect or suspected fraud

items.statement: The contract describes how rejected starting materials, intermediates, bulk and finished products are handled.
items.quote: The contract shall describe the handling of starting materials, intermediate, bulk and finished products, if they are rejected.

items.statement: The contract describes the procedure to follow if contract analysis shows the tested product must be rejected.
items.quote: It shall also describe the procedure to be followed if the contract analysis shows that the tested product must be rejected.

items.statement: The self-inspection programme is designed to detect shortcomings in GMP implementation and to recommend necessary corrective actions.
items.quote: The self-inspection programme shall be designed to detect any shortcomings in the implementation of good manufacturing practices and to recommend the necessary corrective actions.

items.statement: Self-inspections are performed routinely, and may additionally be performed on special occasions such as a product recall, repeated rejections or an announced regulatory inspection.
items.quote: Self-inspections shall be performed routinely, and may be, in addition, performed on special occasions e.g., in the case of product recall or repeated rejections, or when an inspection by the regulatory authorities is announced.

items.statement: The self-inspection team consists of personnel able to evaluate GMP implementation objectively.
items.quote: The team responsible for self-inspection shall consist of personnel who can evaluate the implementation of good manufacturing practices objectively.

items.statement: All recommendations for corrective action from self-inspection are implemented.
items.quote: All recommendations for corrective action shall be implemented.

items.statement: The self-inspection procedure is documented and an effective follow-up programme exists.
items.quote: The procedure for self-inspection shall be documented and there shall be an effective follow-up programme.

items.statement: Written self-inspection instructions are established to give a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.
items.quote: Written instructions for self-inspection shall be established to provide a minimum and uniform standard of requirements.

items.statement: Self-inspection instructions may include GMP questionnaires covering at least: personnel; premises incl. personnel facilities; building and equipment maintenance; storage of starting materials and finished products; equipment; production and in-process controls; QC; documentation; sanitation and hygiene; validation and revalidation programmes; calibration of instruments or measurement systems; recall procedures; complaints management; labels control; and results of previous self-inspections and corrective steps taken.
items.quote: These may include questionnaires on good manufacturing practices requirements covering at least the following items, namely:- (a) personnel; (b) premises including personnel facilities; (c) maintenance of buildings and equipment; (d) storage of starting materials and finished products; (e) equipment; (f) production and in-process controls; (g) quality control (QC); (h) documentation; (i) sanitation and hygiene; (j) validation and revalidation programmes; (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures; (m) complaints management; (n) labels control; and (o) results of previous self-inspections and any corrective steps taken.

not_applicable.text: The purpose of self-inspection is to evaluate the manufacturer’s compliance with good manufacturing practices

items.statement: Management appoints a self-inspection team of experts in their fields who are familiar with GMP.
items.quote: Management shall appoint a self-inspection team consisting of experts in their respective fields who are familiar with GMP.

items.statement: Self-inspection team members may come from inside or outside the company.
items.quote: The members of the team may be appointed from inside or outside the company.

items.statement: Self-inspections are conducted at a frequency set by company requirements but at least once a year.
items.quote: The frequency with which self-inspections are conducted may depend on company requirements but shall be at least once in a year.

items.statement: The self-inspection frequency is stated in the procedure.
items.quote: The frequency shall be stated in the procedure.

items.statement: A report is made when each self-inspection is completed.
items.quote: A report shall be made at the completion of a self-inspection.

items.statement: The self-inspection report includes the results, evaluation and conclusions, and recommended corrective actions.
items.quote: The report shall include the following, namely:- (a) self-inspection results; (b) evaluation and conclusions; and (c) recommended corrective actions.

items.statement: An effective follow-up programme for self-inspection is in place.
items.quote: There shall be an effective follow-up programme.

items.statement: Company management evaluates both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.
items.quote: The company management shall evaluate both the self-inspection report and the corrective actions as necessary.

items.statement: Self-inspections may be supplemented with a quality audit.
items.quote: It may be useful to supplement self-inspections with a quality audit.

items.statement: Quality audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.
items.quote: Such audits may also be extended to suppliers and contractors.

items.statement: The person responsible for quality control, with other relevant departments, is responsible for approving suppliers able to reliably supply starting and packaging materials meeting established specifications.
items.quote: The person responsible for quality control shall have responsibility, together with other relevant departments, for approving suppliers who can reliably supply starting and packaging materials that meet established specifications.

items.statement: Suppliers are evaluated before being approved and added to the approved suppliers' list or specifications.
items.quote: Before suppliers are approved and included in the approved suppliers’ list or specifications, they shall be evaluated.

items.statement: Supplier evaluation considers the supplier's history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.
items.quote: The evaluation shall take into account a supplier’s history and the nature of the materials to be supplied.

items.statement: Where a supplier audit is required, it determines the supplier's ability to conform with GMP standards.
items.quote: If an audit is required, it shall determine the supplier’s ability to conform with good manufacturing practices standards.

items.statement: Enough qualified personnel are available to carry out all tasks for which the manufacturer is responsible.
items.quote: For this reason there must be sufficient qualified personnel to carry out all the tasks for which the manufacturer is responsible.

items.statement: Individual responsibilities are clearly defined, understood by the persons concerned and recorded as written descriptions.
items.quote: Individual responsibilities shall be clearly defined and understood by the persons concerned and recorded as written descriptions.

items.statement: The manufacturer has an adequate number of personnel with the necessary qualifications and practical experience.
items.quote: The manufacturer shall have an adequate number of personnel with the necessary qualifications and practical experience.

items.statement: No individual's responsibilities are so extensive as to present a risk to quality.
items.quote: The responsibilities placed on any one individual shall not be so extensive as to present any risk to quality.

items.statement: Responsible staff have specific duties recorded in written descriptions and adequate authority to carry out their responsibilities.
items.quote: Responsible staff shall have its specific duties recorded in written descriptions and adequate authority to carry out its responsibilities.

items.statement: Duties of responsible staff may be delegated to designated deputies with a satisfactory level of qualifications.
items.quote: Its duties may be delegated to designated deputies with a satisfactory level of qualifications.

items.statement: There are no gaps or unexplained overlaps in responsibilities of personnel involved in applying GMP.
items.quote: There shall be no gaps or unexplained overlaps in the responsibilities of personnel concerned with the application of good manufacturing practices.

items.statement: The manufacturer has an organisation chart.
items.quote: The manufacturer shall have an organisation chart.

items.statement: All personnel are aware of the GMP principles affecting them and receive initial and continuing training relevant to their needs, including hygiene instruction.
items.quote: All personnel shall be aware of the principles of good manufacturing practices that affect them and receive initial and continuing training, including hygiene instruction, relevant to their needs.

items.statement: All personnel are motivated to support establishing and maintaining high quality standards.
items.quote: All personnel shall be motivated to support the establishment and maintenance of high quality standards.

not_applicable.text: (k) calibration of instruments or measurement systems; (l) recall procedures;
not_applicable.reason: list item of sentence started on previous page

A quality audit is usually conducted by outside or independent specialists or a team
The establishment and maintenance of a satisfactory system of Quality Assurance (QA) and the correct manufacture

items.statement: QC laboratories are separated from production areas.
items.quote: QC laboratories shall be separated from production areas.

items.statement: Areas using biological, microbiological or radioisotope test methods are separated from each other.
items.quote: Areas where biological, microbiological or radioisotope test methods are employed shall be separated from each other.

items.statement: QC laboratories are designed to suit the operations performed in them.
items.quote: QC laboratories shall be designed to suit the operations to be carried out in them.

items.statement: QC laboratories have sufficient space to avoid mix-ups and cross-contamination.
items.quote: Sufficient space shall be given to avoid mix ups and cross-contamination.

items.statement: QC laboratories have adequate suitable storage for samples, reference standards (cooled if necessary), solvents, reagents and records.
items.quote: There shall be adequate suitable storage space for samples, reference standards (if necessary, with cooling), solvents, reagents and records.

items.statement: Laboratory design considers suitability of construction materials, prevention of fumes and ventilation.
items.quote: The design of the laboratories shall take into account the suitability of construction materials, prevention of fumes, and ventilation.

items.statement: Laboratories and production areas have separate air supplies.
items.quote: There shall be separate air supply to laboratories and production areas.

items.statement: Biological, microbiological and radioisotope laboratories have separate air-handling units and other provisions.
items.quote: Separate air-handling units and other provisions are needed for biological, microbiological and radioisotope laboratories.

items.statement: A separate instrument room may be provided to protect instruments from electrical interference, vibration, excessive moisture and other external factors, or where instruments must be isolated.
items.quote: A separate room may be needed for instruments to protect them against electrical interference, vibration, contact with excessive moisture and other external factors or where it is necessary to isolate the instruments.

items.statement: Equipment is located, designed, constructed, adapted and maintained to suit the operations performed.
items.quote: Equipment must be located, designed, constructed, adapted and maintained to suit the operations to be carried out.

items.statement: Equipment layout and design minimise the risk of errors and allow effective cleaning and maintenance to avoid cross-contamination, dust or dirt build-up and any adverse effect on product quality.
items.quote: The layout and design of equipment must aim to minimise the risk of errors and permit effective cleaning and maintenance in order to avoid cross-contamination, build-up of dust or dirt, and, in general, any adverse effect on the quality of products.

items.statement: Equipment is installed so as to minimise any risk of error or contamination.
items.quote: Equipment shall be installed in such a way so as to minimise any risk of error or of contamination.

items.statement: Fixed pipework is clearly labelled with its contents and, where applicable, flow direction.
items.quote: Fixed pipework shall be clearly labelled to indicate the contents and, where applicable, the direction of flow.

items.statement: All service pipework and devices are adequately marked, with special attention to non-interchangeable connections or adaptors for dangerous gases and liquids.
items.quote: All service pipework and devices shall be adequately marked and special attention paid to the provision of non-interchangeable connections or adaptors for dangerous gases and liquids.

items.statement: Balances and other measuring equipment of appropriate range and precision are available for production and control and are calibrated to a fixed schedule.
items.quote: Balances and other measuring equipment of an appropriate range and precision shall be available for production and control operations and shall be calibrated according to a fixed schedule.

items.statement: Production equipment is thoroughly cleaned to a fixed schedule.
items.quote: Production equipment shall be thoroughly cleaned according to a fixed schedule.

items.statement: Laboratory equipment and instruments suit the test procedures performed.
items.quote: Laboratory equipment and instruments shall be suited to the testing procedures undertaken.

items.statement: Washing, cleaning and drying equipment is chosen and used so it is not a source of contamination.
items.quote: Washing, cleaning and drying equipment shall be chosen and used so as not to be a source of contamination.

items.statement: Production equipment presents no hazard to products.
items.quote: Production equipment shall not present any hazard to the products.

items.statement: Product-contact parts of production equipment are not reactive, additive or absorptive to an extent affecting product quality.
items.quote: The parts of the production equipment that come into contact with the product must not be reactive, additive or absorptive to an extent that would affect the quality of the product.

items.statement: Defective equipment is removed from production and QC areas, or if removal is not possible, clearly labelled as defective to prevent use.
items.quote: Defective equipment shall be removed from production and QC areas. If this is not possible, it shall be clearly labelled as defective to prevent use.
items.condition: if removal is not possible, label

items.statement: Closed equipment is used whenever appropriate.
items.quote: Closed equipment shall be used whenever appropriate.

items.statement: Where open equipment is used or equipment is opened, precautions are taken to minimise contamination.
items.quote: Where open equipment is used or equipment is opened, precautions shall be taken to minimize the contamination.

items.statement: Non-dedicated equipment is cleaned by validated cleaning procedures between production of different products to prevent cross-contamination.
items.quote: Non-dedicated equipment shall be cleaned according to validated cleaning procedures between being used for production of different pharmaceutical products to prevent cross-contamination.

items.statement: Current drawings of critical equipment and support systems are maintained.
items.quote: Current drawings of critical equipment and support systems shall be maintained.

items.statement: Materials used for cleaning, equipment lubrication, pest control and similar operations do not come into direct contact with the product.
items.quote: No materials used for operations such as cleaning, lubrication of equipment and pest control shall come into direct contact with the product.

items.statement: Where possible, such cleaning, lubrication and pest-control materials are of a suitable grade (such as food grade) to minimise health risks.
items.quote: Where possible, such materials shall be of a suitable grade (e.g., food grade) to minimise health risks.

items.statement: All incoming materials and finished products are quarantined immediately after receipt or processing until released for use or distribution.
items.quote: All incoming materials and finished products shall be quarantined immediately after receipt or processing, until they are released for use or distribution.

Materials include starting materials, packaging materials, gases, solvents, process aids, reagents and labelling materials.

items.statement: For small volume injectables, a minimum of 150 square metres for the basic installation and 100 square metres of ancillary area is recommended.
items.quote: A minimum area of one hundred and fifty square meters for the basic installation and an ancillary area of one hundred square meters for Small Volume Injectable are recommended.
numbers: one hundred and fifty square meters

items.statement: For large volume parenterals, 150 square metres each for the basic installation and for the ancillary area is recommended.
items.quote: For Large Volume Parenterals, an area of one hundred and fifty square meters each for the basic installation and for ancillary area is recommended.
numbers: one hundred and fifty square meters

items.statement: These injectable manufacturing areas are partitioned into suitable enclosures with airlocks.
items.quote: These areas shall be partitioned into suitable enclosures with airlock arrangements.

items.statement: Separate areas are provided for formulations for external use and for internal use to avoid mix-up.
items.quote: Areas for formulations meant for external use and internal use shall be separately provided to avoid mix- up.

items.statement: The packaging materials area for large volume parenterals is at least 100 square metres.
items.quote: Packaging materials for large volume Parenteral shall have a minimum area of one hundred square meters.

items.statement: Manufacture of large volume parenterals in plastic containers or pouches by automatic form-fill-seal or semi-automatic blow-moulding fill-seal machines may be divided into separate areas or rooms: water management, solution preparation, container moulding-cum-filling and sealing, sterilisation, quarantine, visual inspection and packaging.
items.quote: The whole operation of manufacture of large volume parenteral preparations in plastic containers including plastic pouches by automatic (all operations in one station) Form-Fill-Seal machine or by semi-automatic blow moulding, filling-cum-sealing machine may be divided into following separate areas or rooms, namely- (1) Water management area; (2) Solution preparation area; (3) Container moulding-cum-filling and sealing area; (4) Sterilisation area; (5) Quarantine area; (6) Visual inspection area; and (7) Packaging area.
items.condition: LVP in plastic containers by FFS or BFS

items.statement: For FFS/BFS large volume parenterals, the water management area is recommended to have an RO or EDI water treatment unit, a multi-column distillation unit with heat exchangers, a thermostatically controlled water storage tank, transfer pumps, and service lines supplying user areas through a continuously circulating pipework loop.
items.quote: The following equipment is recommended for different above mentioned areas namely- 1. Water management area- (1) RO or Electro-deionisation (EDI) water treatment unit; (2) Distillation unit (multi column with heat exchangers); (3) Thermostatically controlled water storage tank; (4) Transfer pumps; and (5) Service lines for carrying water into user areas through continuously circulating pipe work loop.
items.condition: LVP in plastic containers by FFS or BFS
